speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; let's start by describing exactly how your balance and coordination are affected in your daily life. Have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, speech, or eye movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of appearing "drunk" while walking and unilateral clumsiness suggest cerebellar involvement. On what side of your body are you experiencing the most significant weakness or coordination loss, and have you noticed any specific changes in your speech, such as slurring or a scanning pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The combination of recent onset cerebellar ataxia (gait and limb) and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly specific for this JC virus reactivation. We need to confirm the demyelinating lesions in the white matter immediately. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
